deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the neighbouring pages: X is a set, later a topological space. F is a family of 'tame' subsets satisfying axioms a)–d), presumably closure under finite Boolean operations and closure of closures. F_0 is the subfamily of closed members, and on the previous page F_0 alone determines the coarsest compatible topology. This page adds a new axiom.

Axiom f): for every A in F that is locally closed (A = B − C with B, C in F_0), A has only finitely many connected components, and each component belongs to F. Since there are finitely many components and each is closed in A, each is also open in A.

Consequence 1: connectedness becomes intrinsic to F_0. A locally closed A in F is connected iff there is no splitting A = A' ⊔ A'' with A', A'' in F, both nonempty and both relatively closed in A. 'Relatively closed in A' means a trace on A of an element of F_0. So connectedness can be tested without the topology of X, using only F_0. This defines '𝓕_0-connectedness', and f) can be read as a condition on F_0 alone.

Consequence 2: if F_0 satisfies a condition (φ) (not spelled out on this page), every A = B − C with C ⊂ B in F_0 decomposes as a finite disjoint sum of members of F. These pieces are relatively closed in A and are F_0-connected.

Consequence 3: suppose the open members of F form a basis of the topology. Then f) implies every A in F is locally connected. Grothendieck says this holds at least for locally closed A, and adds that the restriction is in fact unnecessary. Argument: for x in A, intersect A with basic F-open neighbourhoods U. Each U ∩ A is again locally closed and in F, so it has finitely many components, each open in it. The component containing x is then a connected open neighbourhood of x.

Purpose: this is part of an axiomatics for 'topologie modérée' (tame topology). The aim is a family of subsets with finiteness and connectedness properties like semialgebraic or subanalytic sets, specified purely combinatorially by the closed tame sets F_0. The next page goes on to finite partitions and stratification-like conditions.
errors: The aside that the local-closedness restriction is 'inutile' is not proved here. It needs every A in F to be a finite union of locally closed members of F (presumably axiom c) or d)). Gluing local connectedness across pieces then needs a small argument (shrinking U to drop pieces whose closure misses x). This is plausible but not written.

Consequence 1 (connected iff no nontrivial splitting inside F) silently uses that F is closed under finite unions, so that one component and the union of the others are both in F. This is presumably axiom a).
Condition (φ) on F_0 is invoked without being stated on this page.

ideas.what: Axiom that every locally closed tame set has finitely many connected components, each itself tame.
ideas.modern_name: Finiteness of (definably) connected components in o-minimal structures / tame geometry; known theorem for semialgebraic and subanalytic sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Semialgebraic case: Whitney, Łojasiewicz (1950s–60s). Subanalytic case: Hironaka, Gabrielov. o-minimal case: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (1984–86).
ideas.where_published: Programmatic only: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 'topologie modérée'; Récoltes et Semailles mentions it. No detailed axioms published.

ideas.what: Connectedness expressed purely through the lattice F_0 of closed tame sets, independent of the ambient topology.
ideas.modern_name: Definable connectedness (no partition into two nonempty definable relatively clopen sets)

ideas.what: If tame open sets form a basis, the finite-components axiom implies tame sets are locally connected.
ideas.modern_name: Local connectedness of definable sets in o-minimal / tame structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in o-minimal geometry (van den Dries, 'Tame topology and o-minimal structures', 1998)

missed.claim: In 1974, roughly ten years before o-minimality (van den Dries 1984, Pillay–Steinhorn 1986) and before the Esquisse, Grothendieck sets out tame-topology axioms. He takes a Boolean family of subsets, determined by its closed members F_0, and posits finiteness of components with each component tame. He also observes that connectedness then becomes a purely F_0-internal ('definable') notion. Where Grothendieck takes finiteness of components as an axiom, o-minimality derives it from a one-dimensional condition. The page shows his tame topology was conceived lattice-theoretically, as a property of the family F_0, which is closer in spirit to 'definable topological spaces' and abstract tame topologies than usually acknowledged.
missed.quote: c'est donc là une condition qui ne fait pas intervenir la topol. de X, mais F_0 directement
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents the date and form of Grothendieck's independent tame-topology axiomatics. It is relevant to the history of o-minimality and to current work on abstract or definable topological spaces and tame categories (e.g. Lurie-style constructible sheaf theory on tame spaces).

deep.surprise_reason: Grothendieck's interest in topologie modérée is known from the Esquisse (1984). Seeing an explicit 1974 axiom matching 'finitely many definably connected components' and 'definable connectedness' is a notable early detail. The mathematics itself is elementary and later standard in o-minimal geometry.
